text:
anya: kicking off canary for Nereid-14b (int4). Observed warm-start OOMs when max_new_tokens >= 1024; fragmentation metric jumps and doesn't recover. attaching quick logs.
deploy-bot: Canary created: nereid-14b-int4 @ pool-gamma (12 replicas).
leo: could you paste repro steps and env? GPU type? microbatch?
anya: repro: single-stream chat, target length ~1200-1500 tokens. Seen on Ampere and Hopper VMs. Both microbatch=1 and 2 sometimes hit OOM.
ciara: smells like KV slot churn + allocator free list fragmentation. Similar to earlier 14b int4 cases. Try disabling prefetch on warm starts and force a small eviction threshold.
ben: log extract at OOM:

```
[E] cudaMalloc(blk=1228800000) -> OOM
allocating attn_kv buffer 1.14GiB
post-oom allocator: free_chunks=13, largest_free=64MiB
heap_free_over_time: [2.1GiB, 1.9GiB, 1.5GiB, 400MiB]
```

leo: small/cheap mitigations first: reduce model default max_new_tokens from 1024 -> 512; enable slab_compact_on_eviction; set prefetch=false for warm path.
anya: also propose a short "priming" ping on new instance startup: run a 80-120 token dummy generation to allocate stable KV shapes before accepting user traffic. lowers cold/warm spike.
ciara: batching policy: keep microbatch small for latency, but allow 20ms batching window and a max_concurrent of 2 for burst consolidation. That reduces short-lived alloc churn.
ben: will run an overnight A/B test comparing current config vs proposed:
- control: max_new=1024, prefetch=true, kv_eviction_thresh=0.8, slab_compact=false
- variant: max_new=512, prefetch=false, kv_eviction_thresh=0.6, slab_compact=true, startup_prime=true
run command:
```
./canary_job --model nereid-14b --quant int4 \
  --ctrl_tag=baseline --var_tag=frag-mit --duration=8h \
  --collect alloc_hist:5m --collect frag_metrics:5m --workload=long-gen
```
leo: ensure we capture alloc histograms, free-chunk counts, and per-replica OOM events. Capture sample traces for any OOM.
anya: include quality checks: run 1k conv-bench prompts through each variant and compute Rouge/LLMScore/detokenized differences to catch quantization+config regressions.
ciara: rollout plan if variant looks stable: canary -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% with FP16 fallback if OOM rate > 0.5% or latency P95 regresses > 20%.
ben: starting A/B now. will post morning summary with plots. :thumbsup:
leo: if tail OOMs persist after this, next steps: kernel CPU affinity pinning for allocator thread, patch small page alignment in allocator, or increase eviction aggressiveness per-slot.
anya: i'll reserve 3 spare debug nodes in case we need live heap inspection. ping me if you want them.
ben: results posted 6158962000 (will link).
